issues.legal_issue: A residence requirement for a local dealership intended to provide local employment requires actual residence rather than a legal or familial connection to the locality.
material_facts: The dealership eligibility criteria required applicants to be residents of the district where the dealership would operate, and the stated purpose of that requirement was to provide employment or a source of income to local residents.
The dealership was to be operated by a full-time working dealer, making the dealer’s personal presence at the place of business relevant.

The selected applicant’s claimed connection to the district rested on her marriage to a person with ancestral and other property there; there was no finding that her husband permanently resided there.
The record indicated that the applicant appeared to be a permanent resident of another district, including through her voter registration and receipt of ration there.
issues.conclusion: The residence criterion required actual, de facto residence in the district; a connection arising from marriage or a spouse’s property there was insufficient. The Court set aside the High Court judgment and remanded the appeals for fresh consideration under that interpretation.
issues.legal_principle: The meaning of “residence” depends on the context and purpose of the requirement and may refer to temporary or permanent residence, or to de facto or de jure residence. A local-employment purpose, together with a requirement that the dealership be managed by a full-time working dealer, calls for actual residence rather than a merely legal or familial connection. The Court relied on Sarat Chandra Basu v. Bijoy Chand Mahatab Maharajadhiraj Bahadur of Burdwan (concerning Section 33 of the Registration Act, 1908), Sri Sri Sri Kishore Chandra Singh v. Babu Ganesh Prasad Bhagat, Mst. Jagir Kaur v. Jaswant Singh, Jeewanti Pandey v. Kishan Chandra Pandey (concerning Section 19(ii) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955), and Union of India v. Dudh Nath Mishra.

rule.if: residence_eligibility_appeal and local_resident_criterion and local_employment_purpose and full_time_personal_dealership

predicates.residence_eligibility_appeal: The proceeding challenges a decision about whether an applicant satisfies a residence-based eligibility criterion.
predicates.local_resident_criterion: The selection criteria require an applicant to reside in the locality where the opportunity will operate.
predicates.local_employment_purpose: The residence requirement is intended to provide employment or income to people who live in that locality.
predicates.full_time_personal_dealership: The opportunity requires its holder to work full time and be personally present at the place of business.

issues.definition: When an eligibility appeal concerns a local-resident criterion intended to benefit local residents and requires full-time personal work at the business, the criterion requires actual residence in the locality.
